hypothesis: The native SDIO controller and card layer enumerate functions, build CMD52 and CMD53 requests, and retain state on every error.
conclusion: Passed on the host model; physical SDIO operation is unqualified.
narrative: The register-model fixture checks/sdio-controller.c, run by checks/sdio-controller.py (the runner was removed from the repository), passed with address and undefined-behavior sanitizers. It covered enumeration with two functions, manufacturer inheritance, CMD52 read-after-write, a 20-byte radio identity command, a 512-byte byte-mode read, a 1,024-byte block-mode write and interrupt reassertion. Error cases covered version rejection, reset timeout, clock regression, R5 errors, missing completion events, late completion and an invalid CIS pointer. Focused follow-up cases (select-io, cis-shape and reinit result files) passed for CMD7 informational/error status, partial FIFO callback failure, malformed function-extension tuple shapes and refusal to reinitialize active or faulted objects; the earlier enumeration and transfer evidence was reused, the corrections changed only response-bit and malformed-tuple rejection, and the initialization guard preserved the first initialization path with retained state and callback counts unchanged. A case selected with --case widen covered four-bit widening: refusal of out-of-range divisors and repeated requests, the module callback with the card clock stopped, readback of clock, width, delays and timing mode, a level-sized 128-word read burst from one status sample, and terminal faults when the module change fails or the sample delay no longer matches preparation. results.json identifies the initial direct build and run. The evidence includes compiler, command, source/header hashes and executable identity; freestanding AArch64 object evidence is under aarch64-lifecycle/. The card layer uses the runtime's memset plus the controller API. No physical operations or measurements were performed.
